mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate compresses the discount rate applied to equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as the cost of capital falls.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS declines for 3 consecutive months, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate rises above 5.3% and remains elevated for two consecutive months, it signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce corporate earnings growth expectations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 45% of triggered instances, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in retail sales (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) above their 3-month moving averages indicates strong consumer spending momentum, which drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days through improved corporate earnings outlook.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when both RSAFS and HOUST are above their 3-month moving averages, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of active monetary tightening (FEDFUNDS rising above 4.0%), the increased cost of capital reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as the market prices in higher discount rates.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 45% of periods when FEDFUNDS > 4.0%, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in monthly payroll employment (PAYEMS) above the 3-month average indicates a strengthening labor market that boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when PAYEMS increases for 3 consecutive months, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) falls below 110.0 and remains below for two consecutive months, it signals a contraction in manufacturing output that reduces corporate profits, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 45% of triggered instances, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of strong quarterly GDP growth (GDPC1 above 2.0%) and rising retail sales (RSAFS above its 3-month average) signals sustained economic expansion, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days through elevated earnings expectations.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when both GDPC1 > 2.0% and RSAFS > 3-month average, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 210) coincides with declining industrial production (INDPRO < 110.0), the economy faces stagflation risks that depress equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 45% of periods when CPIAUCSL > 210 and INDPRO < 110.0, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.
